Calculate the electrical resistivity of the wire material in ohm-meters.
Use the wire length L = 0.492 m.
Use the wire diameter d = 1.944 mm, which equals 0.001944 m.
Calculate the circular cross-sectional area using the standard formula A = πd²/4, ignoring any earlier instruction to use A = πd².
Compute the area as A = π(0.001944)²/4 ≈ 2.968×10⁻⁶ m².
Use the wire resistance R = 11.705 Ω.
Compute the resistivity using the formula ρ = R·A/L.
Report the final resistivity value, which is approximately 7.06×10⁻⁵ Ω·m.
